run.question: How do /afk:fix (run by /afk:execute, /afk:preflight and the /afk:bug fixer) and /afk:bug's publisher, fixer and retester run and return their results today, what reaches them, and what breaks if /afk:fix runs as an afk-lite team (a design stop for the human, a builder that leaves uncommitted changes and an OUTCOME: line, a hub that runs Phases 2.5, 3 and 3.5, the unchanged status set) and /afk:bug's publisher, fixer and retester become pane agents that return their result lines through result files, with the fixer returning BUGFIX: blocked on afk-lite's design stop (state S5, the same lane, a push notification, resumed by the developer's answer)? Premise: A blocked /afk:bug fixer is a Turn agent that stops on its blocked result; the developer's answer resumes its harness session in a new pane. Premise: A pane role agent with no pattern runs the model its tier names in PROVIDERS.md; an implementation-tier agent runs the pin. Premise: Under afk-lite the hub starts both reader helpers of /afk:fix, at fix/SKILL.md:23 and :60. Premise: The afk-lite hub surfaces a shifted subtask contract as needs_artifact_sync in the OUTCOME line to its requester. Premise: The contact starts every pane agent, so a chain of requesters adds no nesting level; the runner of /afk:diagnose is a helper. Premise: A pane agent that cannot confirm a live build ends with cannot_reproduce and names the build; only the contact talks to the human. Premise: The team of a /afk:bug fixer starts in the bug's fixer worktree. Premise: In afk-lite the hub names the test edits of escape analysis; the builder makes them, and the verifier proves them red then green. Premise: SETTLEMENT.md:52's diet binds pane briefs and messages, not only subagent prompts. Premise: A pane fixer runs under the team's full-access launch flags, and its write fence holds by convention. Premise: The retester writes only its result file; the main /afk:bug session copies the evidence into the bug directory and records the path.

claims.text: the hit set holds every reference to afk:fix, afk:bug over the name forms this pass searched

Today /afk:fix runs inside its caller's own session as a skill: /afk:execute routes a tier still red after one retry (Step 8), correctness and spec review findings (Step 10) and critical or high adversary findings (Step 10.5) to it, and /afk:preflight routes correctness and spec findings of PF-3 and PF-4 to it. It ends with an `OUTCOME: <status>` line and an `In plain terms:` sentence, never commits, and the caller commits its edits.

What reaches /afk:fix today: the bug key or text from its caller, a Jira digest pulled with tracker_get by an afk-reader helper, the session type read from the cwd's branch and spec dir, and the PRD, SDD, ADR and VERIFICATION-PLAN digests of a second afk-reader helper in Phase 3; Phase 1 runs /afk:diagnose, Phase 2.5 runs ESCAPE-ANALYSIS.md, and Phase 3.5 appends a lesson with `hooks/lesson-append.sh opened ... --writer fix`.

No plugin code or test parses /afk:fix's OUTCOME line or its status tokens: a search of every code directory for `OUTCOME:` and `design_conflict` returned 2 lines, a tooltip text (hooks/lavish-tips.json:64) and a journal classifier (skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/mc/sections/insights.py:24), and the seed found fixed_no_test, cannot_reproduce and needs_artifact_sync only in prose and glossary fixtures. Callers read the line as prose, so keeping the status set leaves no parser to break.

With the status set unchanged, an afk-lite design stop for the human can only come back as `blocked` (fix/SKILL.md:94). /afk:execute Step 8 routes only `design_conflict` to a human path, so the stop ends the subtask as test_fail or build_fail; Steps 10 and 10.5 read no /afk:fix status, so the stop spends rounds until review_fail or adversary_fail; /afk:preflight PF-3 and PF-4 end in park(PF-3: review_stalemate) or park(PF-4: orphan_artifact). No caller carries the stop's design to the human, so these five call sites break; no test pins them.

Given the premise that the afk-lite hub surfaces a shifted subtask contract as needs_artifact_sync in its OUTCOME line, the /afk:execute requester has no route for that status: Step 8 names only design_conflict and otherwise re-runs from Step 8, so the shifted contract is not acted on in that run.

/afk:execute's hard rule reads every verdict from the spawning call's own result and never waits on a completion notification from a child (execute/SKILL.md:135). An afk-lite /afk:fix team returns its OUTCOME: line through a result file, so this rule must change for the /afk:fix route; how the requester learns the file landed is harness runtime that no probe row covers.

A pane agent holds the tracker MCP tools on Claude Code (9 tools, tracker_transitions answered) but not on Codex CLI, where the server registered (`tracker: connected (9 tools)`) and the tools were absent from the model's turn (fail); on both, the tracker server started in the pane's launch directory, and mcp-servers/tracker/server.py:63 reads its adapter kind from config.load(Path.cwd()).

Given the premise that the afk-lite hub starts the reader helper of /afk:fix's Jira intake (fix/SKILL.md:23), that intake breaks on a Codex hub, because a Codex pane agent had no tracker tools in its turn (CONFORMANCE.md:321, fail). On Claude Code the pane agent held them; whether the helper the hub starts holds them is unverified, because row 321 probed the pane agent, not its subagent.

Given the premise that the team of a /afk:bug fixer starts in the bug's fixer worktree, its tracker server reads config with that directory as the root: the tracked .afk/config.yaml and ~/.afk/config.yaml reach it, and the gitignored .afk/config.local.yaml does not, unless worktree.copy lists it (the default copy list is .mcp.json, .claude, .run, .idea).

A pane session fires Stop and runs the plugin Stop gates on both Claude Code and Codex CLI (row 323, pass), while a subagent's end fired only SubagentStop with no gate metrics; in this worktree (92 changed files) the gate run passed the 300 s hook limit on both harnesses. The Stop entry runs the wiring gate with no scope test (hooks/stop-gates.sh:108).

Under afk-lite, each pane member's turn end runs the Stop gates over the shared worktree's uncommitted changes, including what the builder leaves; today /afk:fix inline in the caller's session met them only at the caller's turn end. The verdicts do not change (a builder's new non-test file with no referrer blocks the Stop as it blocked the caller's), but every member turn pays a gate run, which hit the 300 s limit here.

A pane agent resolves the plugin's named agent definitions on both harnesses (row 324), and a pinned model name runs exactly that model on both (row 325). This worktree pins afk-implementor to claude-opus-4-8 (agents/afk-implementor.md:4) and the Codex stub to gpt-5.6-terra (afk-afk-implementor.toml:3); the installed copy the probes ran carries the alias opus and gpt-6-sol, and the Codex reader stub's sandbox_mode read-only did not apply to its sub-agent.
